lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm responsible for one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a 17-year-old son named Alex who lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 17 years old, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college anymore. He did start an apprenticeship though - he's training in Wales.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is important - the rules state that if your child starts an apprenticeship in England, Child Benefit stops. However, you mentioned Alex is training in Wales.

**Can you confirm what type of apprenticeship program Alex is on? Is it specifically a Welsh apprenticeship program, or is it an apprenticeship in England that happens to involve training in Wales?**

Also, **when did Alex start this apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a Welsh apprenticeship program - he's doing his training in Wales, not England. He started it a few months ago, back in September.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is a crucial distinction!

The rules I have specifically state that Child Benefit stops if your child "starts an apprenticeship in England." Since Alex is on a Welsh apprenticeship program (not an English one), this particular rule does not apply to him.

However, there's another rule that states Child Benefit stops if your child "starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training."

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week as part of his Welsh apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working 24 hours or more a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me just confirm a few final details to make my assessment:

1. **Do you live in the UK?**

2. **Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or are you looking to make a new claim?**

3. **Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in England. I'm looking to make a new claim, and no, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I need to give you an **INDETERMINATE** assessment for Alex's eligibility.

Here's why:

The Child Benefit rules specifically state that benefit stops if a child "starts an apprenticeship in England." However, Alex is on a **Welsh apprenticeship program**, not an English one, so this exclusion doesn't directly apply to him.

For 16-19 year olds like Alex, Child Benefit can continue if they stay in "approved education or training." The rules I have access to don't provide clear guidance on whether Welsh apprenticeships (or those in Scotland or Northern Ireland) qualify as "approved education or training" for Child Benefit purposes.

**What I'd recommend:**

You should **contact the Child Benefit Office directly** to clarify whether Alex's Welsh apprenticeship counts as approved education or training. They will be able to give you a definitive answer based on the specific details of his apprenticeship program.

You can reach them by phone or post - their contact details are available through HMRC's Child Benefit service.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
